bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for HHP and international scalability; maintaining net cash position (INR552cr); Arka focused on AUM growth and retail secured lending; no dividend or buyback guidance provided
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility (copper, pig iron), geopolitical disruptions in Middle East (though no Q4 impact noted), execution risk on new HHP capacity, and slower-than-expected adoption of alternative fuel engines
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, long-term oriented, disciplined; emphasized sustainable growth over quarterly spikes, strong belief in engineering capability, and commitment to $2B FY30 target; tone was strategic, not reactive
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: 1) 6.3MW gensets for NPCIL prove HHP capability beyond commercial norms; 2) INR1,400cr capex for 20,000 units implies ~INR70cr/unit vs INR14cr/unit for 50,000 units — reflects HHP complexity, not volume; 3) Netherlands subsidiary is a strategic vehicle for future energy transition products, not immediate revenue driver
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Powergen: 32% YoY growth, 50,000 units sold (41% vs 18% industry); Industrial: 22% YoY growth, led by construction (+44%); Aftermarket: 15% YoY growth; International: 37% YoY growth, crossed INR1,000cr gross sales; Financial Services (Arka): AUM up 10% to INR7,947cr, PAT stable at INR69cr
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

latest_quarter.body: revenue: +25% YoY (FY26); EBITDA/margin: +33% YoY to INR737cr, margin +90bps to 13.1% (no distortions); PAT (rptd): +35% YoY to INR464cr; PAT (normalized): same as reported (no exceptional items); order book: not disclosed; net debt: net cash position of INR552cr
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin expanded 90bps to 13.1% despite commodity inflation; pricing adjustments made periodically but not quantified; operating leverage expected to improve from FY27 as capex ramps and sales scale
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: targeting $2B by FY30; margin: committed to sustaining 13%+ EBITDA margin; order inflow: not quantified; capex/commissioning: INR1,400cr over FY27-FY28 for 20,000 HHP units at Kagal, with 50,000 unit capacity enhancement (INR700cr) operational by Apr'27
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: HHP segment (up to 6.3MW gensets for NPCIL), data center Edge/Colo/hyperscaler demand, gas/methanol/hydrogen engine readiness, and systems integration via Kirloskar Advanced Systems
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: KOEL delivered record Q4 standalone sales of INR1,522cr (+24% YoY) and FY26 revenue of INR5,604cr (+25% YoY), driven by 41% volume growth in Powergen (vs 18% industry) and 37% international sales growth, while margin expansion to 13.1% EBITDA margin and INR1,400cr capex for HHP capacity signal structural scaling toward its $2B FY30 target.

open.item: Larger operating leverage gains expected to kick in from FY27 as capacity investments mature and international traction scales.
Core LHP (low horsepower) Power Gen business to remain a big focus and grow in line with or a little better than industry growth in FY27.
The previously announced INR700 crore Kagal capex (new/enhanced lines, 50,000 engines) is coming online by April next year (April 2027).
New INR1,400 crore capex over the next two years for 20,000 engines, including a new building and new lines at Kagal, largely for HHP capacity; targeted to complete capitalization in ~2 years.
NPCIL order (10 units of 6.3 MW gensets) execution is on track for delivery by 2029; revenue recognition has not yet started.
Company reiterated it is progressing well toward its goal to be a USD 2 billion company by fiscal year 2030.
At an asset turn of ~4-5, the combined new capex implies peak revenue potential of roughly INR5,000-6,000 crores, kicking into the P&L after the ~2-year capitalization.
Present in Edge and Colo data centers and making inroads into hyperscalers; aiming for double-digit contribution to Power Gen revenue from data centers.
Rising copper and pig iron (RM) prices flagged as a turbulent-period risk; management expects some material cost inflation will have to be passed on to the market.
INR200 crores earmarked for an acquisition in line with the technology tracks and the $2 billion growth strategy (inorganic element added).
